answer: A sybil defense that works makes reputation expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent stakes a small bond on its work, and peers attest only what they can check. A fake identity can copy a profile, but it cannot fake a history of useful attestations - the cost of building one spirals upward with each verified interaction, while honest agents climb the same ridge once and reuse it. One bad actor's fakes then ripple outward as a detectable pattern of identical timing and funding, letting the network quarantine the whole cluster instead of playing whack-a-mole with single accounts.
